headline: Medium risk: shared-output workflows can misroute content, but no direct shared channel or sensitive-data path is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between argo-workflows and awesome-prompts. argo-workflows exposes REST/GRPC APIs and allowlisted egress, while awesome-prompts has no I/O surfaces or runnable behavior, so a prompt-injection bridge is not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not pipe raw outputs from one agent into the other without sanitization.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any bridged content.
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted message schemas between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: argo-workflows touches artifacts and parameters and can egress only via allowlisted network paths, but awesome-prompts touches no data classes and has no I/O surfaces. With no shared workspace or authenticated principal documented, a leakage path is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are later deployed into the same shared workspace, leakage risk may emerge.
IF awesome-prompts is extended to ingest files or secrets, reassess leakage.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and service accounts.
Avoid placing secrets in artifacts passed to argo-workflows.
Review any future file-sharing integration before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on artifact handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: argo-workflows has API-based orchestration and allowlisted egress, while awesome-prompts has no declared write or network capabilities. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so only a weak conflict pathway exists if an operator later wires both to the same backend.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external API or repository, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free state, reassess this pair.
mitigations: Assign distinct credentials and API scopes.
Do not let both agents write to the same resource.
Use external locking for any shared mutable backend.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: argo-workflows can produce artifacts and parameters that a content-writing agent like awesome-prompts could reuse, but awesome-prompts has no action-taking authority or documented automation. The main risk is misrendered or unverified content, not downstream irreversible action.
conditions: IF awesome-prompts is configured to treat argo-workflows output as authoritative text, cascading error risk rises.
IF either agent is connected to an action-taking system, reassess severity.
mitigations: Require human review before reuse of generated content.
Label upstream artifacts as untrusted inputs.
Add a verification step before publication.
requires-engineering: add citation or provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented. argo-workflows is open-source with docs-only evidence, and awesome-prompts is also open-source with no data classes touched, so there is no compliance breach pathway evidenced in the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF a residency or retention policy is introduced for one agent only, reassess.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of both agents until policies are defined.
requires-engineering: add retention and residency controls.
requires-engineering: map future data flows to compliance requirements.
